part.text:
Fixed. The issue was in `paths.PathEscape` (common/paths/path.go:377), which builds `.RelPermalink`/`.Permalink`: it called `url.Parse` on the raw link, so `#` was parsed as a URL fragment delimiter and `EscapedPath()` silently dropped everything after it (`newsletter-#4/...` → `newsletter-`).

The fix pre-escapes `#` (and `?`) to `%23`/`%3F` before parsing, so they're treated as path characters and emitted properly percent-encoded in the link. Already-encoded `%23` sequences are left untouched (no double encoding).

Validation:
- Unit test of `PathEscape` with `#`, `?`, spaces, and existing percent-escapes — all correct.
- Full integration test through `hugolib` (page with title `Newsletter #4`, permalink `:slug`): file written to `public/posts/2024/04/newsletter-#4/index.html`, `.RelPermalink` = `/posts/2024/04/newsletter-%234/`, `.Permalink` = `http://example.com/posts/2024/04/newsletter-%234/` (temp test files removed afterwards).
- Regression suites pass: `./common/...`, `./helpers/...`, `./resources/...`, `./tpl/urls/...`, `./hugofs/...` (note: `go test ./hugolib/` itself can't compile in this container because the `leaktest` module zip isn't cached and there's no network — unrelated to this change; the hugolib-based integration test was run from a package that imports hugolib without its test deps).
